what_its_for: Degarelix is used to treat advanced prostate cancer. It works by lowering the amount of testosterone in your body. Prostate cancer cells often need testosterone to grow, so reducing testosterone helps slow or stop the cancer from growing.
how_to_take: Degarelix is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous injection) in your belly area (abdomen). A healthcare provider such as a doctor or nurse will give you this injection in a clinic or doctor's office. You will NOT give this injection to yourself at home. The injection is usually given in two separate shots side by side in your belly during your first visit, and then one shot at each visit after that.
dosing: Your first dose (starting dose) is usually two injections of 120 mg each (240 mg total) given on the same day. After that, you will receive one injection of 80 mg every 28 days (about once a month). Always keep your scheduled appointments so your doses are not missed. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on how well the medicine is working for you.
missed_dose: Because this medicine is given to you by a healthcare provider, it is very important to keep all of your scheduled clinic appointments. If you miss or need to reschedule an appointment, call your doctor or clinic right away to set up a new appointment as soon as possible. Do not try to skip or delay doses on your own, as this could allow your testosterone levels to rise and may let the cancer grow.
storage: Degarelix is stored and prepared by your healthcare team at the clinic. You do not need to store this medication at home. If for any reason you are given any supplies to take home, keep them at room temperature (below 86°F or 30°C), away from light, heat, and moisture, and out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Tell your doctor about all medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, especially any heart medicines or medicines that affect heart rhythm (such as certain antibiotics, antifungals, or antidepressants), because degarelix can affect your heart's electrical activity. Avoid activities that could increase your risk of falls or broken bones, as this medicine can weaken your bones over time. Do not drink excessive amounts of alcohol. Do not donate blood while taking this medicine and for some time after stopping it.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: chest pain, fast, slow, or irregular heartbeat or pounding in your chest; shortness of breath; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, itching, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or trouble breathing; severe pain, redness, swelling, or a lump at the injection site; signs of low blood sugar such as dizziness, sweating, or shakiness; hot flashes that are very bothersome; bone pain or a broken bone; depression or mood changes; difficulty urinating or blood in your urine; numbness or tingling in your arms or legs; or any new or unusual symptoms that worry you.
when_it_works: Degarelix works quickly. Your testosterone levels should drop significantly within 3 days of your first injection. However, it may take several weeks to months before you notice improvements in your symptoms or before your doctor sees changes in your lab tests (such as PSA levels). Continue taking this medicine as scheduled even if you feel well, because it is working in your body even when you cannot feel it.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): This medicine is commonly used in older men and is generally safe, but your doctor will watch you closely for side effects such as bone loss, heart rhythm changes, and falls. Patients with heart problems: Tell your doctor if you have a history of heart disease, heart failure, or irregular heart rhythm (QT prolongation), as degarelix may increase the risk of heart rhythm problems. Patients with liver or kidney problems: Dose adjustments are usually not needed for mild to moderate liver or kidney problems, but your doctor should know about your full medical history. Bone health: Because this medicine lowers testosterone, it can weaken your bones over time (osteoporosis). Your doctor may recommend calcium, vitamin D supplements, or bone-strengthening medicines. Diabetes: This medicine may affect blood sugar levels, so your doctor will monitor you closely if you have diabetes.
